Q0139

“The Master said: When you see the worthy, think of equaling them;…” — Confucius (Analects 4.17)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Analects 4.17. Theme: cultivation.

Quotes / Confucius / Q0139

English

The Master said: When you see the worthy, think of equaling them; when you see the unworthy, examine yourself within.
Thinker Confucius
School Confucianism
Source Analects 4.17
Theme Cultivation
Another quotation More from this thinker

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Analects 4.17 and files it under Confucianism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Confucius

Confucius (Kong Qiu, 551–479 BCE) taught in the late Spring and Autumn period amid the Zhou order’s political fragmentation. Born in the state of Lu, he briefly held local office and then spent years seeking rulers who would adopt ritual-based, virtue-centered government.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Mencius and Al-Ghazali), cultivation is framed through Confucianism and Islamic Philosophy. Some passages define cultivation; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through cultivation.

Concepts in this quote

Cultivation
Cultivation appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat cultivation as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
